study_identification_part.si_4_title: Charting brain growth and aging at high spatial precision

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study assembled data from 82 sites. Named public datasets include: ABCD (21 sites), ABIDE (sites GU, KKI, NYU, USM), ADHD-200 (sites KKI, NYU), CAMCAN, CMI-HBN (sites CBIC, RU, SI), CNP (2 sites), HCP-Aging (4 sites: MGH, UCLA, UM, WU), HCP-Development (4 sites: MGH, UCLA, UM, WU), HCP-Early Psychosis (4 sites: BWH, IU, McL, MGH), HCP-Young Adult, IXI, NKI-RS, Oasis2, Oasis3, PNC, TOP, UK Biobank (2 sites: ukb-11025.0, ukb-11027.0). Additional single-site datasets come from University of Michigan (CWS, IMPs, MLS, MTwins, SAD, SZG), UC Davis, Kings College London, Amsterdam UMC (delta), SRPBS (CIN, COI, KTT, KUT, HKH, HRC, HUH, SWA), AOMIC (1000, PIPO2), ATV, SWU_SLIM, and several OpenNeuro datasets (ds001734, ds002236, ds002330, ds002345, ds002731, ds002837). A separate transfer validation set was drawn from OpenNeuro (ds000115, ds000222, ds003416, ds003469, ds003653). Overall, well over 10 distinct named datasets were used, qualifying as MULTI-DATASET.

King's College London ... and Amsterdam University Medical Center"

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Data were split into equal-sized training (N=29,418) and test (N=29,418) sets stratified by site. Clinical data (N=1,985) was held in the test set. A separate transfer validation set (N=546, 6 sites from OpenNeuro) was used to demonstrate generalizability to new unseen sites. The mQC subset (N=24,354, 59 sites) was used for validation against manual quality checking.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "Equal sized training and testing data sets (split half) were created using scikit-learn's train_test_split function, stratifying on the site variable." ... "To show generalizability of the models to new data not included in training, we leveraged data from OpenNeuro.org ... to create a transfer data set (six sites, N=546, Supplementary file 3)." ... "The clinical validation sample consisted of a subset of the full data set"

model-1.model-name: warped Bayesian linear regression model (cortical thickness and subcortical volume)

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: One normative model was built using warped Bayesian Linear Regression with likelihood warping (PCNtoolkit v0.20). The full sample of 58,836 healthy controls from 82 sites was split into equal training (N=29,418) and test (N=29,418) sets. Note: clinical samples (N=1,985) were a subset of the overall data (from sites that had both controls and patients), meaning these controls were present within the 58,836 total. Additionally, a manually quality checked (mQC) subset of 24,354 participants from 59 sites was used for validation (train=12,177, test=12,177).

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The overall-phase mean and SD are computed as weighted mean and pooled SD from the train (N=29,418; mean=46.9, SD=24.4) and test (N=29,418; mean=46.9, SD=24.4) sets. Since both halves have identical N and identical reported statistics, the overall weighted mean = 46.9 and pooled SD = 24.4. The age range of 2-100 is stated in the abstract. Median and IQR are not reported. The mQC subset (N=24,354) has: train mean=30.2, SD=24.1; test mean=30.1, SD=24.2; overall weighted mean ≈ 30.15, pooled SD ≈ 24.15.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "we assembled a reference cohort of neuroimaging data from 82 sites (N=58,836; ages 2-100)" ... Table 1: Training set "46.9, 24.4", Test set "46.9, 24.4"

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Sex info for the overall phase was inferred from the train and test percentages. Train: 51.1% F of 29,418 = ~15,033 F, 48.9% M = ~14,385 M. Test: 50.9% F of 29,418 = ~14,974 F, 49.1% M = ~14,444 M. Overall: F = 15,033 + 14,974 = 30,007 (51.0%), M = 14,385 + 14,444 = 28,829 (49.0%). The Table 1 'All' row for the full sample does not directly report sex percentages. The mQC subset overall: Train 50.2% F of 12,177 ≈ 6,113 F; Test 50.4% F of 12,177 ≈ 6,137 F; Overall F ≈ 12,250 (50.3%), M ≈ 12,104 (49.7%).
